sentence: This project studies how gut bacteria survive antibiotics, persist in the gut and become resistant, using sequencing and microbiology.
This project offers immune tests and technical support to measure how the immune system responds to cancer.
This project studies how the cup shape of a cell sensor that detects mechanical forces changes how neighboring sensors work.
This project prepares a package to qualify a clinician-reported instrument that measures how severe attenuated positive symptoms are in patients at high risk for psychosis.
This project studies what controls symmetric and asymmetric divisions of hematopoietic stem cells, focusing on how RNA methylation guides them.
This project studies how differences in human DNA change the function of brain cells in Alzheimer's disease, using cell culture and human tissue.
This project studies how a molecular machine called the Integrator complex controls the amount of RNA made, and why the spliceosome makes circular RNAs.
This project uses CRISPR screening to find the regulators that make breast cancer cells fuse with each other.
This project develops a blood test that detects and isolates myeloma cells, as a way to diagnose multiple myeloma without painful bone marrow biopsies.
This project develops a gene therapy for oculocutaneous albinism type 1 and uses it to learn why the neural retina develops improperly.
This project builds a mouse model for cancers linked to Epstein-Barr virus, including lymphoma, head-and-neck cancer and gastric carcinoma.
This project develops a subzero solution and machine perfusion method to keep human and porcine kidneys preserved for much longer.
This project provides measurement tools that guide individual treatment and help find combination treatments that work together.
This project builds a machine learning platform that predicts which synonymous codons help industrial hosts make more protein under stress.
This project studies the HIV reservoir and immune features of people who caught HIV while taking pre-exposure prophylaxis.
This project studies how localized neuronal hyperexcitability in gliomas links to seizure and tumor growth, using spatial proteomics.
This project uses metagenomic sequencing and machine learning to study how the oral microbiome develops in infants and relates to early childhood caries.
This project offers help with statistics and machine learning so researchers can analyze data from medical records, retinal imaging and tissue imaging.
